title: Sell Mineral Rights in Lumberport, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Lumberport, WV
metaDescription: Lumberport, Harrison County mineral owners: West Fork River-corridor tracts, legacy wells, and undivided heir interests through the Clarksburg courthouse.
heroLead: Lumberport sits along the West Fork River in Harrison County, on ground that carries decades of production history predating today's horizontal wells.
intro: Lumberport's location along the West Fork corridor put it within reach of gas development going back to the mid-1900s, and much of the mineral acreage in and around town has changed hands — through both sale and inheritance — multiple times since the original severance.

sections.heading: River-corridor tracts and their production history
paragraphs: Acreage near the West Fork River in and around Lumberport was among the earlier-developed parts of Harrison County, with wellbores from several distinct drilling eras sometimes present on a single tract. Sorting out which lease governs current production — and whether older leases were properly released before newer ones were signed — is a common title task here.

sections.heading: Undivided interests and courthouse records
paragraphs: Like much of rural Harrison County, Lumberport-area mineral interests are frequently held as undivided fractional shares among multiple heirs. The Harrison County Courthouse in Clarksburg holds the deed and will books that establish exactly what percentage each heir holds, which is the starting point before any sale or lease decision.

sections.heading: Surface access and mineral ownership are separate questions
paragraphs: Because Lumberport sits along an active river corridor with multiple wellbores nearby, some owners assume their surface use rights and their mineral ownership are the same thing — they aren't. West Virginia treats the mineral estate and the surface estate as separately ownable, and a lease or sale of your mineral interest doesn't grant or restrict any surface rights you separately hold or don't hold.

Confirming which estate you actually own — surface, minerals, or both — is part of the same courthouse review used to establish your chain of title, and it directly affects how a buyer values your interest.

faqs.question: My Lumberport tract has wells from different eras — does that complicate my title?
faqs.answer: It can, particularly if older leases weren't formally released before newer ones were executed. A title review sorts out which lease currently governs and confirms your royalty is calculated correctly.

faqs.question: How do I find my exact percentage share of a Lumberport family interest?
faqs.answer: A courthouse records check tracing the deed and will books from the original severance forward will establish your current percentage.

faqs.question: Can I sell an undivided interest in Lumberport without the rest of my family agreeing?
faqs.answer: Yes, your individual fractional share can be sold independently of your co-owners.

faqs.question: If I only own minerals and not the surface, can I still sell?
faqs.answer: Yes, a mineral interest without surface rights is sellable on its own, just like a combined surface-and-mineral interest.
